How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can follow to call the **“get nodes list”** API from your own script or via `curl`.  
I’ll walk through each part so you know exactly what needs to change when you switch environments.

---

### 1️⃣ What You Need First

| Item | Why it matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Cisco Nexus Dashboard IP** (`192.168.11.33`) | Target device address |
| **Fabric Name** (`PEK-ACI`) | Query filter – will be inserted into the URL |
| **Authentication Token / Credentials** | Most APIs require a Bearer token or Basic Auth header |

> *If you’re not sure where to find the auth token, check the “Security → Tokens” section in the dashboard UI.*

---

### 2️⃣ Construct the Endpoint URL

Your base template:

```
https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}
```

Replace `{ip}` & `{fabricName}`:

```text
https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI
```

That’s the full URI you’ll hit.

---

### 3️⃣ Authentication Header

Most Nexus dashboards issue JWT tokens. Example header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
```

*Tip:* If you only have username/password, you may first POST `/auth/login` to receive a token.

---

### 4️⃣ Making the Call

#### A) Using `curl`

```bash
curl -k \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -X GET \
"https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI"
```

- `-k`: skip SSL verification (use only in dev/test).
- Replace `YOUR_JWT` with the actual token.

#### B) In Python (requests)

```python
import requests

BASE_URL   = "https://192.168.11.33"
ENDPOINT   = "/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes"
FIBER_NAME = "PEK-ACI"

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}

params = {"fabricName": FIBER_NAME}

response = requests.get(
    url=f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", 
    params=params, 
    headers=headers, 
    verify=False          # set True in production!
)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

> **NOTE:** Set `verify=True` once you move out of development; otherwise you risk insecure connections.

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Test With Our Tool

(Only works if you supply a valid token.)

```json
{
  "function":"requests_get",
  "arguments":{
      "url":"https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI",
      "fabricName":"PEK-ACI"
  }
}
```

*(This would trigger our internal helper to perform the same GET request.)*

---

### 6️⃣ Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Verify token hasn’t expired; re‑authenticate. |
| **404 Not Found** | Double‑check the exact path—sometimes there’s a typo in `/cisco-nir/...`. |
| **SSL errors** | Either add `--insecure/-k` flag or install the proper CA cert on the client machine. |
| **Wrong Fabric Name** | Ensure case sensitivity matches the backend config. |

---

### TL;DR Code Snippet

```bash
curl -k \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \
-X GET \
"https://${IP}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=${FABRIC}"
```

Where:
- `$IP="192.168.11.33"`
- `$FABRIC="PEK-ACI"`

Happy querying! 🚀
